summary: Wen-ling Jane is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Jane earned a PhD at Columbia University, attested in 2009, studying under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and teacher Geshe Lobsang Jamspal.

Wenbiao Mai specializes in Indology and linguistics. Mai completed a PhD at Peking University and also studied at the University of Hamburg and Kyoto University. In 2013, Mai was attested as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong.

Wendi L. Adamek works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Adamek earned a PhD at Stanford University by 1998, held a post at Barnard College in 2008, and served as Numata Chair in Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary.

Wendy Doniger is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned an MA and PhD from Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and a D.Phil. from Oxford under Robert Charles Zaehner, before joining the University of Chicago faculty in 1978.
Wendy Palace is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. Palace earned a PhD at Durham University under the doctoral supervision of David Sweet.

Wenhui Yang (1837–1911) was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar. He founded the Jinling Scriptural Press (1897), the Jetavana Hermitage (1908), and the Buddhist Research Society (1910), serving as the latter's head.

Wenjie Duan (1917–2011) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the Central Academy of Fine Arts (~1940–1945), he held multiple posts at the Dunhuang Academy from 1946, serving as its director in 1991.
Wenjie Qin is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Qin earned a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Wei-ming Tu.

Werner Abraham (1936–2024) was a linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Vienna in 1965. His academic career included posts at the University of Groningen from 1971, the University of Tübingen, and several visiting professorships.

Werner Sundermann (1935–2012) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He held posts at the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (~1970–1992), Humboldt University of Berlin, and Free University of Berlin (~1993–2000).
Wes Borton is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Borton studied under Derek F. Maher at East Carolina University and later studied at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

Whalen Lai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Harvard (~1969–1975) and held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1973–1976) and University of California, Davis (~1976–2009).

Whitney Cox is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Virginia and University of Chicago. Cox held academic posts at the University of Chicago, attested in 2003 and becoming a professor around 2013.

Wijesinghe Sugathadasa Karunaratne (1928–1986) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. After completing a PhD at SOAS/University of London (~1952–1956), he held academic posts at the University of Ceylon, University of Peradeniya, and University of Kelaniya.

Wilburn Hansen is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. Hansen pursued a master's program at the University of Colorado Boulder and completed further studies at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

Wilfred Cantwell Smith (1916–2000) was a religious studies scholar who earned a PhD from Princeton (-1948). He held major positions at Forman Christian College (1940–1946), McGill University (1948–1951), and Harvard University (1964–1973, 1978–1985).

Wilfrid Sellars (1912–1989) was a philosopher educated at Michigan, Buffalo, and Oxford. He held teaching posts at Iowa (1938–1946), Minnesota (1947–1958), and Yale (1958–1963), before serving as a professor at the University of Pittsburgh (1963–1989).

Wilhelm Deecke (1831–1897) was a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate at Leipzig University (1848–1849). He later served as director or head at Ernestinenschule, Gymnase Jean Sturm, Gymnasium Buchsweiler, and Lycée Lambert.

Wilhelm Dilthey (1833–1911) was a philosopher who studied at Heidelberg and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the University of Basel (~1866–1868), Kiel University (~1868–1871), University of Breslau (~1871–1882), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1882–1905).

Wilhelm Geiger (1856–1943) was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who earned his PhD and Habilitation at Erlangen-Nuremberg under Friedrich von Spiegel. He served as professor at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1891) and the University of Munich (1920–1924).
